tasks.title: AWS lane A: storage and credentials
tasks.brief: Inspect media/config.py, media/services/storage.py, processing/config.py, processing/worker/storage.py, recovery stores, database roles/migrations. Exact static-key assumptions, ECS temporary credential tokens and refresh incl presign, source grants, multipart/CORS/expiry behavior, native task role least privileges, separate storage/data ownership, smallest adapters. Focus storage/security, leave networking/release to others.

tasks.title: AWS lane B: placement, network and state
tasks.brief: Inspect deploy Dockerfiles, compose/local/docker-compose.yml(active), nginx configs, PG bootstrap, existing deployments vs accepted AWS plan. Task/container roles/sizing/readiness, DNS replacement and nginx re-resolution/Cloud Map DNS billed requests, dynamic EC2 public IP wake, CloudFront methods/cache/headers/cookies/TLS interpretation, S3 endpoint vs external signed traffic policy, state EBS exports, full shutdown gaps. Assess origin-TLS proposal honestly. No provisioning.

tasks.title: AWS lane C: worker lifecycle and capacity
tasks.brief: Inspect processing worker entrypoint/supervisor/tasks, Redis/RQ publication, SQL leases/fencing, recovery, release/drain paths. Existing --burst suitability and empty queue exit, bounded manual starts(max3 pending+running), interruption/retry/drain/rollback behavior, task-accounting and orphan prevention; late queue arrivals/recovery ownership. Optional automation separate. Keep proven local lifecycle and rejected38/39 intact.

tasks.title: AWS lane D: delivery, clients and evidence
